focus: Q3 Executability by a DeepSeek writer: exact targets, current anchors, atomic tasks, runnable proofs, acceptance mapping and rollback across phases 001–005.
answeredQuestions: Q3 Executability by a DeepSeek writer: does every task name exact files, make one change, carry a proving command, map to an acceptance criterion, and carry a rollback? Which tasks are vague?

label: [CONFIRMED] Escaped-pipe alternation in ripgrep proof commands does not match either surface name, so phase 002 and phase 003 leak checks can return a false zero.
[DOCUMENTED] The five task files do not consistently map implementation tasks to AC IDs or provide per-task rollback instructions; the plans mostly leave rollback at phase level.

[DOCUMENTED/INFERRED] Several tasks combine broad multi-file edits or separate actions: phase 002 T014/T028–T031/T034/T068/T058, phase 003 T002/T027/T030, phase 004 T003/T006/T009/T010/T011/T013/T016, and phase 005 T003/T007/T017. A DeepSeek writer could omit a file, mix generated and manual edits or publish a partial result.

[DOCUMENTED/CONFIRMED] Phase 005 T005 contains a literal <the ten paths> placeholder in its proof, and T012's grep row count also matches the AC-ID header, so the proof is incomplete and its expected count is off by one.
[CONFIRMED/INFERRED] Sampled numeric anchors match the current HEAD, while the long phase 004 edit catalogue still depends on description-based OLD-text matching that should be checked at each use.
